summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a complex history of fibrosing mesenteritis, recurrent small bowel obstructions, and G-tube dependence was readmitted one week after discharge due to recurrent fevers and positive blood cultures for coagulase-negative staphylococcus. The infection was traced to her port-a-cath and PICC line, both of which were removed. She completed a four-week course of IV vancomycin, with follow-up cultures remaining negative. During the admission, she developed new-onset severe abdominal pain, prompting multiple imaging studies and an enteroscopy, which showed partial mechanical obstruction from adhesions but no surgical cause. Her pain was managed with a multimodal regimen including gabapentin, morphine, and amitriptyline. She also experienced transient acute kidney injury due to dehydration from high G-tube output, which resolved with IV fluids. Her G-tube was replaced due to leakage. She was discharged home on TPN, bolus IV fluids, full liquids, and a revised medication regimen, with plans for follow-up blood cultures and potential port reinsertion.
